t.E511.agn: In 2019, EFSA re-evaluated E 507, E 508, E 509 and E 511 together; it stated that acute toxicity was low and that there was no concern regarding genotoxicity or carcinogenicity, and used a reference value of 40 mg/kg body weight per day for chloride. It has been reported that this value may be slightly exceeded in high consumers in some age groups (toddlers, children, adolescents), but it was concluded that there was no safety concern at the reported use levels.
t.E511.body: In the gastrointestinal tract it dissociates into chloride and the accompanying ions. Chloride taken in with food is almost completely absorbed along the intestine and distributed to organs and tissues; the amount in the body is regulated by balance mechanisms, and it is excreted mainly in urine, and also in sweat and faeces.
t.E511.found.1: May be used at quantum satis (as much as needed) in many foods in the EU
t.E511.prod: It is obtained by dissolving magnesium oxide, hydroxide or carbonate in hydrochloric acid and crystallising it.
t.E511.regx.0: Chlorides E 507–E 511 re-evaluated together; no safety concern at the reported use levels (reference for chloride 40 mg/kg bw per day).
t.E511.regx.1: Group I additive; in the salt category, permitted at quantum satis only in sea salt.
t.E511.summary: Magnesium chloride. Used as a coagulant (nigari) in tofu making.
t.E511.what: It is a mineral salt used as a consistency regulator and stabiliser; it is also permitted in sea salt. Chloride and magnesium are natural minerals also taken in with food.
